name: Redan Shoals
description: Redan Shoals is a warm oceanic world distinguished by its remarkably shallow global ocean, averaging only three hundred meters in depth across most of its surface. Extensive shoal systems create vast areas where the ocean floor is visible from the surface, the water a luminous turquoise over white sand and pale limestone. The planet's reef systems grow in distinctive V-shaped formations -- redans -- that point into the prevailing currents, their angular profiles creating sheltered lagoons in their lee.

The shallow waters ensure that sunlight reaches the ocean floor across most of the planet, driving photosynthetic productivity of extraordinary magnitude. The water is warm, clear, and teeming with life at every scale, from microbial films coating every surface to large pelagic fauna that patrol the channels between shoal systems. Tidal sand flats emerge during low tide across thousands of square kilometers, creating temporary land bridges between reef formations.

The redan reef formations support the planet's highest biodiversity concentrations, their V-shaped structures creating distinct ecological zones on the exposed, sheltered, and apex faces. The largest redans span several kilometers, their apex points visible from orbit as pale V-shapes against the deeper blue of the inter-shoal channels. Marine fauna has adapted to navigate the complex reef geometry, with species specialized for each zone of the redan structure.

Redan Shoals' shallow, productive waters make it one of the most biologically rich ocean worlds in the cataloged systems. Aquaculture potential is immense, and the redan reef structures provide natural frameworks for cultivation. The planet's breathable atmosphere and mild climate further enhance its appeal, though the near-total absence of dry land presents habitation challenges. Floating settlement designs adapted to the shallow, calm waters are under development by several colonial planning groups.
